intro: Mozambique has a long Indian Ocean coast where Swahili traders and Portuguese colonists once ruled.

chapters.title: Coastal trade
text: Swahili and Arab traders set up towns along the coast from about the 900s, trading gold from inland kingdoms like Mutapa. The Island of Mozambique gave the country its name.

chapters.title: Portuguese rule
text: Vasco da Gama arrived in 1498, and Portugal ruled for nearly 500 years, using forced labour on plantations. In 1964 FRELIMO began a war for independence.

chapters.title: Independence and war
text: Mozambique became independent in 1975 under Samora Machel. A civil war with RENAMO from 1977 to 1992 killed around a million people. Peace brought growth, but since 2017 an insurgency has hit the northern province of Cabo Delgado, and disputed 2024 elections led to deadly protests.

keyTerms.meaning: The liberation movement and ruling party.
The former rebel movement, now a party.
